packageRules.description: The go directive of go.mod is the floor of the toolchain: never automerge
Rust (extractor/rust): keep the ranges in Cargo.toml and move only Cargo.lock
Dart (extractor/dart): bump the constraints in pubspec.yaml together with pubspec.lock
The Dart SDK of CI moves with package:analyzer: never automerge

The pinned Rust nightly moves only through the custom manager rust-nightly, which moves rust-toolchain.toml, isolate.go and the README together. The built-in rust-toolchain manager moves rust-toolchain.toml alone (the constant in isolate.go would no longer match it), and the global automerge would merge it

The Dart SDK of ci.yml (sdk: of setup-dart) moves through the custom manager only. The built-in github-actions manager finds the same value, which made two branches for one update (renovate/github-actions and renovate/dart-3.x) and put dart into the automerge group of GitHub Actions
The pinned Rust nightly moves with the extractor (rustc_public is unstable): never automerge. The source gives only the newest date and no release time, so minimumReleaseAge would wait for ever

customManagers.description: Tool versions in scripts/build-release-archives.sh, marked with a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment above `name=vX.Y.Z` (go-licenses). The same in ci.yml is covered by the shared preset

Dart SDK version in ci.yml: `sdk:` of setup-dart (the model-diff job) and `DART_SDK:` of the jobs that hold it in an env (test, cost-warn). All of them move together (one branch). scripts/dev-setup.sh holds the pin with its checksums too: it checks that it agrees with ci.yml and fails when it does not, so that the bump of the checksums is not forgotten

The pinned Rust nightly (nightly-YYYY-MM-DD) in every file that has to carry it: rust-toolchain.toml, isolate.go, the install commands of extractor/rust/README.md. The prose of the documents points at rust-toolchain.toml and carries no date; if one is written, this manager moves it too. Not in docs/adr, docs/history, docs/issues (records of what was decided or seen then) and not in the tests (their dates are test data)

rust-nightly.description: The date of the newest Rust nightly: one line, e.g. 2026-11-23 (one release for Renovate)
